records.title: Design & Analysis of JPDAF Tracker with AI-Enabled Maneuvering Models
records.funder: Prince Sultan Defense Studies and Research Center (PSDSARC)
records.description: This project, which aims to enhance radar target tracking through the integration of artificial intelligence, was accepted by the Prince Sultan Defense Studies and Research Center (PSDSARC) and awarded funding of 277,150 SAR for a one-year duration. The project aims to advance target tracking capabilities by incorporating AI into the Joint Probabilistic Data Association Filter (JPDAF) algorithm. It utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)/Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance performance in complex, high-acceleration scenarios while also extending functionality to bistatic and passive radar systems for increased accuracy and adaptability.

media.alt: Animated radar tracking plot showing a target trajectory and JPDAF tracking behavior.

records.title: Vehicle Access Automation
records.funder: Deanship of Postgraduate Studies and Scientific Research at Qassim University
records.description: Automation is a key goal of Saudi Vision 2030; however, most vehicle gates in the country remain manual, resulting in inefficiencies and security risks. This project proposes a sustainable, computer vision–based gate automation system with strong anti-spoofing capabilities. We detect the nearest car using IoU and extract three features: car make/model, Saudi license-plate recognition, and face recognition. These are matched against a database, followed by a final decision via a linear SVM. The prototype source page reports approximately 94% accuracy.

media.alt: Animated vehicle-access demonstration with a vehicle detection region.

records.title: Design and Implementation of a Novel and Robust Automated Attendance System
records.funder: Partially Funded by the Innovation and Intellectual Property Center at Qassim University
records.description: This project presents a smart and robust automated attendance system using computer vision and deep learning. Designed for educational institutions, it tracks student attendance in real time by capturing multiple images during class, recognizing faces to mark presence, detect latecomers, and ensure students remain throughout the session. The system uses YOLOv8 for person detection and InsightFace for face recognition. The supplied source reports 96.30% accuracy.

media.alt: Automated attendance recognition demonstration in a classroom.

records.title: Design and Implementation of a Robust Anti-Spoofing System for Vehicle Gate Access Using Recent Artificial Intelligence Techniques
records.funder: Logistically Supported by the Innovation and Intellectual Property Center at Qassim University
records.description: The system automates vehicle gate access using computer vision and machine learning. It detects the nearest vehicle via intersection over union (IoU), then extracts car make, license plate, and driver face using specialized models. These features are matched against an authorized database and a linear SVM makes the final access decision. The source reports 97% vehicle classification, 93.1% license-plate recognition, 57% face recognition, and 97% overall classification accuracy.
